review_cost.rationale: A round of changes: fix the cache poisoning, de-duplicate the home page's client code, remove dead code and tighten a few types. Everything else approves as-is.

findings.issue: Module-level promise singletons (speciesIndexPromise, typeInfoPromise, generationInfoPromise, pokedexDataPromise) are never cleared on rejection, so a transient API failure on first hit poisons every page render with a cached rejection until the process restarts.
findings.suggestion: Reset the singleton in a .catch() (e.g. speciesIndexPromise = api(...).then(...).catch((e) => { speciesIndexPromise = undefined; throw e; })) so the next request retries.

findings.issue: The entire 1,025-species dataset is embedded as JSON on every page load and the client script (~185 lines) reimplements filtering, pagination, humanization and card markup that already exist server-side, creating a second copy of the view that will drift from the Astro implementation.
findings.suggestion: Let the server own rendering: submit filters via a plain form GET (or link navigation with the ClientRouter), and keep a single card/filter implementation; if instant search is required, extract the shared logic into one module imported by both.

findings.issue: getPokemonMovesData is a 90-line function that mixes data fetching with presentation policy (English labels, method ordering, default sort order) inside the shared data module.
findings.suggestion: Return raw move/method data and move labels and ordering into the page or a small presentation helper next to statLabels in [name].astro.

findings.issue: set:html={JSON.stringify(payload)} will terminate the script element early (and could inject markup) if any API string ever contains '</script>'.
findings.suggestion: Escape it: JSON.stringify(payload).replace(/</g, '\\u003c'), or pass data via a data- attribute / fetch on load.

findings.issue: 404.astro is unreachable dead code: the [...path].astro catch-all already matches every unmatched URL and renders its own not-found page.
findings.suggestion: Delete 404.astro, or move the not-found rendering into it and have the catch-all and per-page handlers share it via a component.

findings.issue: strict:false combined with ~40 ': any' annotations means API shapes are unverified and typos in property access fail silently at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Extend 'astro/tsconfigs/strict', define interfaces for the PokeAPI payloads used (species, pokemon, move, type), and use them in api<T>.

findings.issue: 'export const prerender = false' is repeated on every page even though output:'server' already makes on-demand rendering the default.
findings.suggestion: Remove the redundant declarations (or, if the explicitness is wanted, note it once in the config/README rather than per page).

findings.issue: Changing the Game select triggers window.location.assign — a full page reload — where a plain <form method="get"> around the select would work without JavaScript.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the select in a native GET form pointing at the current path, or use the ClientRouter for a soft navigation.

summary: A competent, current-version Astro app: correct routing, status handling and components, with a genuinely good shared data layer that needs one real robustness fix (poisoned promise caches). The home page is the weak spot, duplicating the server render in ~185 lines of inline JS that ships the whole dataset and will drift from the Astro implementation. I'd request one round of changes — cache retry, home-page de-duplication, dead-code and typing cleanup — then merge.
